comment: Owned by the license review. Notices that cmux-tui npm packages and PyPI wheels ship beside the Rust crate notices (package_notices.py). libghostty_vt names the ghostty-next commit of vt-link-graph.json; a bump needs new texts here. musl is linked into the Linux musl binaries. windows_gnu is the static runtime of the x86_64-pc-windows-gnu binaries for the one reviewed toolchain (gcc_build, gcc_version, mingw_w64_version, crt); package_notices.py check-windows-toolchain and check-windows-binary fail another. darwin is the review of the Darwin binaries (no musl-derived code in their real link); package_notices.py check-darwin-binary fails a binary that gains some.

musl.source: musl-1.2.5/COPYRIGHT in https://musl.libc.org/releases/musl-1.2.5.tar.gz (sha256 a9a118bbe84d8764da0ea0d28b3ab3fae8477fc7e4085d90102b8596fc7c75e4). Rust 1.95.0 builds its self-contained musl from musl 1.2.5 (src/ci/docker/scripts/musl.sh); the lib/libc/musl/COPYRIGHT of Zig 0.16.0 and of Zig 0.17.0 is byte-identical.

libghostty_vt.license_tree: collect-ghostty-licenses.py tree of the cmux-next source archive dry run 42004729138 (SOURCE-MANIFEST.json ghostty_revision 383b27d73, no unresolved packages). The texts are byte-identical to the 7d43bb68b ones: Ghostty LICENSE, highway (N-V-__8AAGmZhABb...) LICENSE, LICENSE-BSD3, debian/copyright, wuffs (N-V-__8AAP5JWgCG...) LICENSE, LICENSE-APACHE, LICENSE-MIT and uucode LICENSE.md have the same sha256 in that tree. The upstream sync moves uucode to a new Zig package hash (deps.files.ghostty.org tarball of uucode ea6214973) with the same LICENSE.md, so only its owner key and source change. 850bb9849 (fork PR #84) changes only src/renderer/ReflowPreview.zig, src/renderer.zig, src/benchmark and the CI workflow, so the license texts do not change. 1740c4452 (fork PR #85) changes only src/terminal and src/termio Zig files, its C header and docs, so the license texts do not change. 538a3e2ef (fork PR #86) changes only src/renderer/Thread.zig and src/renderer/Metal.zig, so the license texts do not change. 8379ecc8a (fork PR #90, upstream #15111 and #15121 picked onto 538a3e2ef) changes only src/terminal, src/benchmark and src/synthetic Zig files (one new file, src/synthetic/cli/Hyperlink.zig, no package), so the license texts do not change. b3a5ebfdf (release/cmux-538a3e2e-resize-p0-22, the RESIZE hold release: 7a372c740, fork commits 8c1eec2eb..7a372c740 on 538a3e2ef, merged with 8379ecc8a) changes only include/ghostty.h, src/apprt/structs.zig, src/renderer (Metal.zig, generic.zig, metal/Target.zig), src/terminal/Terminal.zig, src/termio/Termio.zig and src/termio/stream_handler.zig against 8379ecc8a (no package, no build.zig.zon), so the license texts do not change. a0975fd8c (release/cmux-gi-pin-sync-2, five upstream Ghostty commits picked onto b3a5ebfdf) changes only src/terminal Zig files (PageList.zig, Screen.zig, render.zig), no file and no package added, so the license texts do not change.

windows_gnu.toolchain: MinGW-Builds x86_64-15.2.0-release-posix-seh-ucrt-rt_v13-rev1 (https://github.com/niXman/mingw-builds-binaries/releases/download/15.2.0-rt_v13-rev1/x86_64-15.2.0-release-posix-seh-ucrt-rt_v13-rev1.7z, sha256 029bd02b5bce7c10fd9476165b3fe178239fe1838ad62516b5c3e0921bb283cf): GCC 15.2.0, mingw-w64 runtime 13.0.0 (v13.x branch, UCRT, posix threads, SEH). The GitHub windows-2025 image installs it at C:\mingw64 (toolset mingw 15.*, runtime ucrt); cargo links with its gcc and lld.

evidence: PE imports (all four): only Windows system DLLs and the UCRT API sets (api-ms-win-crt-*); no libwinpthread-1.dll, libgcc_s_seh-1.dll, libstdc++-6.dll or msvcrt.dll. All runtime code is static.

Toolchain: one .comment ident 'GCC: (x86_64-posix-seh-rev1, Built by MinGW-Builds project) 15.2.0'; rustc 1.95.0 (59807616e); Zig 0.16.0; LLD 20.1.8. MinGW-Builds rt_v13 builds the mingw-w64 v13.x branch with patch 9002-v13 (exit wrappers, public domain); its _mingw_mac.h says 13.0.0.

Symbol-to-object mapping (COFF symbol table against the archive members of that toolchain): mingw-w64 crt2.o (crtexe.c: mainCRTStartup, atexit), libmingw32.a (gccmain, pseudo-reloc, tlssup, tlsthrd, pesect, crt_handler, merr, usermatherr, natstart, CRT_fp10, dllargv, wildcard, x*mode, cinitexe, exit_wrappers), libmingwex.a (delayimp, loadcfg, mingw_matherr), libucrt.a extras (ucrt_fprintf, ucrt_vfprintf, local_stdio_printf_options, __p___initenv, ucrt_amsg_exit) and UCRT import stubs. Every one of these sources is marked public domain (DISCLAIMER.PD) or carries no header; pseudo-reloc.c says 'THIS SOFTWARE IS NOT COPYRIGHTED'. COPYING.MinGW-w64-runtime.txt is the file mingw-w64 provides for binaries statically linked with its runtime.

GCC 15.2.0 runtime: crtbegin.o (__gcc_register_frame) and libgcc_eh.a unwind-seh.o (_Unwind_*, _GCC_specific_handler; Rust's panic unwinder); possibly libgcc ___chkstk_ms. GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1: the exception allows any terms for the combined Target Code (rustc/LLVM is an eligible compilation process), and the binaries are GPL-3.0-or-later anyway (LICENSE carries the GPL text). COPYING.RUNTIME is included as a courtesy notice.

Not linked: winpthreads (no pthread_* or winpthread symbol, no DLL import; its COPYING is not needed), libstdc++ (__cxa_pure_virtual and __glibcxx_assert_fail resolve to simdutf's own weak stubs in ghostty-next pkg/simdutf), LLVM compiler-rt and libunwind (this is the GNU target, not gnullvm).

Zig compiler_rt (in libghostty-vt): memcpy/memset/strlen, __divti3/__udivti3, __chkstk and the math functions ceil/floor/exp/expf/log/logf/log2/fmod/round/roundf/trunc/truncf resolve to compiler_rt.* at the same addresses. Zig's LICENSE covers compiler_rt; its math files say 'Ported from musl' (MIT), so the Windows notice also carries musl's COPYRIGHT.

libghostty-vt for x86_64-windows-gnu: vt-link-graph.json target x86_64-windows-gnu, regenerated on Testbox tbx_01m45qv05kdd7cpx1g9qk973fn (the four other targets came out byte-identical). Zig emits CodeView for Windows, and its file checksums name only files with line records: highway, wuffs, pkg/highway, pkg/simdutf, pkg/wuffs, Zig std, compiler_rt, libcxx headers; uucode (inlined lookups and comptime tables) is missing, so package_notices.py names every package that any target links for Windows. Zig lib/libcxx header code is Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception, whose exception needs no notice for code embedded in object form.

Rust crates: the x86_64-pc-windows-gnu closure adds winapi-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu 0.4.0 (MinGW import libraries, MIT/Apache-2.0), which ships no license file; reviewed.json now stores winapi-rs's root LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE at its publishing commit 9497609ef44c.

Zig 0.17.0 (ghostty-next a6b9048e9, 2026-11-04): run 41861545663 artifact cmux-tui-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu passes check-windows-binary (no GCC ident but the reviewed one) and still links musl-ported compiler_rt math (compiler_rt.exp, exp2, floor_ceil, fmod, log, log2, round, trunc); the Windows notice keeps musl's COPYRIGHT. The other runtime evidence above is from the Zig 0.16.0 build of run 37288140319.
review.limits: The runner image pins MinGW 15.* by toolset, not one build. check-windows-toolchain (build-windows job, before linking) fails another GCC build, mingw-w64 version or msvcrt, and check-windows-binary (package job) fails a binary that names another GCC build, so a new toolchain needs a new review. The review covers x86_64-pc-windows-gnu only (no aarch64 Windows target is built).

review.decision: NO MUSL TEXT: the Darwin packages link no musl-derived code (Zig 0.17.0, ghostty-next a6b9048e9)
review.reviewer: license review agent for the ghostty-next upstream sync (PR manaflow-ai/cmux#35478); engineering review, not attorney review
review.artifact: GitHub Actions run 41861545663 (cmux-tui.yml workflow_dispatch, 72b34da97, ghostty-next a6b9048e9, Zig 0.17.0): artifacts cmux-tui-aarch64-apple-darwin (cmux-tui ccfb3bb32927f62e..., cmux-tui-hook 0770eed04cf35285...), cmux-tui-x86_64-apple-darwin (cmux-tui 4e2af72ab80d4030..., cmux-tui-hook 9b4e4cafbb2f9d5e...), cmux-relay-aarch64-apple-darwin (3cf2a56ed6830...) and cmux-relay-x86_64-apple-darwin (65b0c3d78fc02...). Its package job failed only on compiler_rt.float_from_int, which this review adds. Previous review: 2026-10-05, Zig 0.16.0, run 37295065948.
evidence: Zig 0.17.0 source (zig-0.17.0.tar.xz from ziglang.org, sha256 b6c7f1728f043700d6529bac980800792f824256a9d2f1839b3d62beed0b8abd). Sources that say they are ported from musl: compiler_rt cos, exp, exp2, fma, floor_ceil, fmod ('heavily inspired by MUSL fmodl'), log, log10, log2, rem_pio2*, round, sin, sqrt, tan, trig, trunc; std/math acos, acosh, asin, asinh, atan, atan2, atanh, cbrt, cosh, expm1, expo2, gamma, ilogb, log, log1p, sinh, tanh, complex/*; std/Io/Threaded.zig writeResolutionQuery (DNS); std/Thread.zig LinuxThreadImpl freeAndExit (Linux only). Every 'ported from / inspired by / copied from musl' line is the same in Zig 0.16.0 (zig-0.16.0.tar.xz, sha256 43186959edc87d5c7a1be7b7d2a25efffd22ce5807c7af99067f86f99641bfdf).

compiler_rt modules in the binaries: float_from_int (__floatuntidf on arm64, __floattidf on x86_64), powiXf2 (ported from LLVM compiler-rt powisf2.c), ssp, udivmod. Zig 0.17.0 merged 0.16.0's floattidf.zig and floatuntidf.zig wrappers into compiler_rt/float_from_int.zig; its floatFromInt is 0.16.0's bit-manipulation code (only Int -> @Int changed), uses no std.math function and names no musl origin. None of the four modules is a musl port. No std.math symbol.

Math functions are imported from libSystem: _cbrt, _cos, _cosf, _exp, _exp2, _fmod, _log, _log10, _log2, _pow, _sin, _tan (arm64) and also _ceil, _fma, _round (x86_64). compiler_rt's musl-ported math is not in the link.

Inlined code: ghostty-next a6b9048e9 still reaches std.math.cbrt only through terminal.color.LAB.fromRgb from the export ghostty_color_palette_generate, which no Darwin package binary links (cmux-tui has 96 other _ghostty_ symbols). A scan for musl cbrtf's constants (movz 0x19f2 then movk 0x2a51 or 0x2651, lsl 16; or the 32-bit immediates) finds 0 in every Darwin package binary and 10 in the iOS app binary of cmux-ci job 88f465baffd86abba2529c18, which has the code.
Zig Io in the binaries uses Io.failingNetLookup; no Io.Threaded DNS symbol.
Rust std's compiler_builtins carries libm (musl-derived); rustc's COPYRIGHT-library.html, which the notices include, covers it.
review.limit: check-darwin-binary sees symbols, not inlined code: it catches the known entry (ghostty_color_palette_generate), musl-ported Zig functions that keep a symbol, and every compiler_rt module outside the reviewed list. A new musl-ported call that is inlined into another libghostty-vt function needs a new review; a new Zig version always does (data_problems).
